items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section X, List of Answers on Topics 21:1
items.html: It was already explained above, in Answer 107, that every lower one comes out from the externality of the screen in the upper one. It was also explained there that this distinction applies only to the aspect of the Katnut of the upper one, which is the aspect of the bottom Hey in Einayim, where the vessel of Galgalta is then considered its HGT, and the vessel of Einayim its NHY. Now, the lower one comes out only from the externality of that Katnut. And even though the lower one comes out only after the Gadlut of the upper one, in which the vessel of Einayim, which was the aspect of NHY, has already risen and become HGT, it was nevertheless explained there that the Katnut is not absent even at the time of Gadlut, but becomes an externality to the Partzuf of Gadlut, see there. It is thus found now as well that the lower one comes out from the aspect of NHY and the aspect of the vessel of Einayim of the upper one, which are considered the ten Sefirot of Malchut, since all of NHY is the aspect of Malchut and the ten Sefirot of ending, where the place of the screen is, as is known. It follows that the lower one comes out from the Malchut that is in the externality of this NHY, since the coarseness in the screen is the aspect of the bottom Hey and Malchut that are in the NHY of the upper one, and the lower one comes out from the externality of this bottom Hey, meaning it comes out from the externality of the Malchut that is in the ten Sefirot of the externality of the NHY of the upper one. (p. 913, Item 83)
